title: Oxygen‐Stable Electrochemical CO 2 Capture using Redox‐Active Heterocyclic Benzodithiophene Quinone

compounds.name: benzodithiophene quinone (BDT-Q)
compounds.quote: We demonstrate that benzodithiophene quinone (BDT-Q), a heterocyclic quinone, exhibits high stability in electrochemical carbon capture processes with oxygen-containing feed gas.

compounds.name: anthraquinone (AQ)
compounds.quote: A systematic comparison with a well-studied anthraquinone (AQ)[14,34–36] under identical conditions using an H-cell indicates a high oxygen stability of BDT-Q relative to that of AQ with an electron utilization of 0.83.

conditions.quote: A solution of 10 mM of BDT-Q in dimethylformamide (DMF) was utilized, with the addition of 0.1 M tetrabutylammonium perchlorate (TBAClO4) as a supporting electrolyte.
All the CV experiments were conducted using a 10 mM BDT-Q/AQ in 0.1 M TBAClO4 as a supporting electrolyte dissolved in DMF, with a scan rate of 100 mV/s.
The cathodic chamber was equipped with graphite felt as a working electrode and 25 mM BDT-Q in 5 mL of DMF containing 0.25 M TBAClO4 as a supporting electrolyte.
The cathodic chamber was equipped with graphite felt as a working electrode and 25 mM BDT-Q in 5 mL of DMF containing 0.25 M TBAClO4 as a supporting electrolyte.
The cathodic chamber was equipped with graphite felt as a working electrode and 25 mM BDT-Q in 5 mL of DMF containing 0.25 M TBAClO4 as a supporting electrolyte.
The Gibbs free energies (ΔG) of electron transfer and the CO2 binding steps were calculated using Density Functional Theory (wB97M-V/def-2-tzvpd) with SMD solvent model.
